q: What CBAM figure should a buyer use for steel from a Durgapur blast furnace plant?
title: Durgapur steel: the CBAM figure
short: Ask the plant for its actual embedded emissions per tonne of the product you buy, calculated under the CBAM method. A blast furnace and converter route usually lands around two tonnes of CO2 per tonne of crude steel. Default values apply only if actual data is missing, and they are set high on purpose.
audience: EU importers and Indian exporters of plates, sections, wheels and other steel from integrated plants in the Durgapur and Asansol belt

ul: Direct emissions from coke making, sintering, the blast furnace and the converter.
Precursors such as pig iron and slabs, attributed through the production chain.
Electricity is reported but not charged for steel goods.

p: Request the installation data in the Commission's communication template for the reporting period, with the production route and the product's CN code. Check it matches the invoice quantities.
The default values in the 2025 implementing regulation apply, with a mark up in later years, which usually costs more than real data.
